questions.prompt: A manager bans the use of AI tools on the team due to data security concerns but does not provide approved alternatives. What is the most likely outcome?
choices: Team members will stop using AI and productivity will remain stable
Team members will use AI anyway but hide it, creating shadow use with no quality standards or oversight
The ban will prompt the company to accelerate approved tool rollout
Productivity will temporarily decrease but will improve once the team adapts to working without AI
questions.explanation: Banning tools without providing alternatives drives use underground. Shadow AI use is worse than visible use — the manager loses the ability to set quality standards, catch errors, or help when something goes wrong. Governed use is safer and more effective than prohibition.

questions.prompt: A manager notices that team communications sent to senior leadership are starting to read with a detectable AI-generated pattern — formal hedging, certain sentence structures — with no apparent human editing. What does this signal and what should the manager do?
choices: This is acceptable because AI-generated writing is often clearer than human writing
The manager should ban AI use in external communications
The review step before sending is being skipped; the manager should address the process, not single out individuals
The team should use different AI tools that generate less detectable text
questions.explanation: AI prose patterns in unedited outbound communications are a sign that the human review step is being skipped. The fix is a process norm — explicit review required before any external communication — not a ban or a tool change. Addressing the process protects quality without penalizing the use of useful tools.

questions.prompt: A manager used AI to draft a Q3 planning document that they then substantially edited and reviewed. Their director asks who wrote the document. What is the most appropriate response?
choices: Say they wrote it, since they edited and reviewed it and it reflects their thinking
Decline to answer since AI assistance is a private workflow choice
Say AI drafted it and they reviewed and revised it — this is accurate and there is nothing to hide
Explain in detail which specific sentences were AI-generated and which were written by the manager
questions.explanation: Transparency about AI assistance, when asked directly, is the right standard. There is nothing wrong with using AI to draft a document you then owned through editing and review. Being comfortable saying so models the honesty you want your team to practice. Claiming sole authorship when AI was meaningfully involved sets a norm of concealment.
